titulo: From the cradle to the grave
intro: The stages of life, from pregnancy and birth to old age and death, in neutral and in careful language.
p.embarazada.nota: False friend: it never means embarrassed.
p.hacerse mayor: to grow up; to get old
b1.texto:
**Before and at birth.** **Quedarse embarazada**, **el embarazo**, **estar embarazada de seis meses**, **dar a luz**, **el parto**, **nacer**. **La maternidad** and **la paternidad** are both the condition and the leave from work.

**The ages.** Each one has a noun and an adjective:

- **la niñez** / **la infancia**: un niño
- **la adolescencia**: un adolescente
- **la juventud**: un joven
- **la madurez**: una persona madura
- **la vejez** / **la tercera edad**: un anciano, una persona mayor

Spaniards avoid **viejo** for people. **Mayor** is the polite word: **una señora mayor**, **las personas mayores**.

**The verbs of change.** **Crecer**, **madurar**, **hacerse mayor**, **envejecer**, **jubilarse**. Many end in **-ecer**, with a **-zc-** in the first person: **envejezco**, **crezco**.

**Death.** The neutral verb is **morir**. In the news and in formal speech it is **fallecer**, and the noun is **el fallecimiento**. After death: **el entierro**, **el funeral**, **enterrar** or **incinerar**, **la tumba**, **el cementerio**. In a crime story the body is **el cadáver**.

**Useful phrases.** **A los veinte años** se fue de casa. **De joven**, vivió en París. **De mayor** quiere ser médico. **Con el paso de los años**…
b2.f0: At the start of the twentieth century, life expectancy at birth in Spain was under forty; today it is over eighty.
b2.f1: That change was due above all to fewer deaths during childbirth and childhood, as well as improvements in living conditions and health care.
b2.f2: At the same time, the population is ageing: a growing share is over sixty-five.
b2.f3: This makes us rethink old age, which can last several decades for many people.
b2.f4: Some older people live alone and need more everyday support.
b2.f5: Ageing with dignity depends on health, autonomy, companionship and access to suitable services.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, why did life expectancy rise so much?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Dejaron de morir tantos niños en el parto y durante la niñez.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Early retirement is a distractor; the question asks why life expectancy rose.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what does growing old with dignity depend on most?
b5.o0.refuerzo: Depende menos de la medicina que de la compañía.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The text does not mention it.
b7.pregunta: Which word would a newspaper use for murió?
b8.o0.refuerzo: Verbs in -ecer take -zc- in the first person.
b9.o0: When she grows up she wants to be a vet.
b9.o1: She wants to be an older vet.
b9.o1.explicacion: De mayor: when one is grown up.
b9.o2: The mayor wants to be a vet.
b10.pregunta: Complete: some die without anyone knowing.

b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an essay on the ageing of the population and its consequences for society.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Talk aloud about which stage of life you think is the best and what worries you about growing old.
b9.o0.explicacion: De mayor means when grown up, used to say what someone wants to be later.
